thermal.limitation: All accepted bridge rail power is treated as local heat. Reference heatsink data do not predict this assembly.

findings.title: VDD transient margin remains open
findings.evidence: The selected 1.5 A to 3 A step reaches 1.08308 V at the low regulator corner. The matching release reaches 1.18521 V at the high corner, before ripple.
findings.action: Measure both load-step directions at the bridge pads. Obtain compatible TPS62903 closed-loop results. Evaluate capacitance, interconnect inductance and regulator response together.

findings.title: Power cycling does not guarantee a bridge reset
findings.evidence: 68 of 96 passive cycle cases never reach the guaranteed 0.8 V reset-low level before power returns.
findings.action: Evaluate reset discharge and multi-rail supervision. Capture VCCH, VCCL, VDD and RST# during short interruptions and during USB attach with ATX off.

findings.title: Rapid 12 V return exceeds the modeled pulse envelope
findings.evidence: The forced-collapse model reaches 170.3 A forward current. The blocking-source model still reaches 163.2 A. The recorded pulse ceiling is 70 A.
findings.action: Evaluate gate reset or controlled restart. Measure the actual PSU return ramp. Keep live card insertion outside the operating envelope until a separate review.

findings.title: The 3.3 V switch still has hot shutdown and restart findings
findings.evidence: 9 of 130 scenarios exceed the estimated equivalent-pulse SOA screen. All scenarios settle, which does not establish SOA margin.
findings.action: Evaluate faster turn-off and restart control. Measure current and VDS during enable cycles and supply return. Check the trajectory at the measured switch temperature.

findings.title: Cooling must cover the accepted power allowance
findings.evidence: The bridge rail budgets sum to 5.62 W. A 35 C ambient requires thetaJA at most 9.79 C/W if all this power becomes local heat.
findings.action: Use a defined heatsink and airflow fixture for the first board. Measure package temperature under sustained traffic. Reference thermal data alone cannot qualify the board.

findings.title: Signal integrity still needs complete channel models
findings.evidence: All twelve differential channels have reduced-network sensitivity results. Package, connector, cable/card and receiver models remain incomplete. No valid eye or BER pass exists.
findings.action: Obtain wideband connector and package models where available. Measure link training, negotiated speed, error counters and sustained transfers across cables and endpoints.

findings.title: VCCL retains the separate 3 A conductor finding
findings.evidence: The 80 C mesh screen gives a 14.52 mV upper drop at 3 A against the 8 mV project budget. The accepted planning load is 1 A.
findings.action: Retain the 1 A design assumption explicitly. Measure rail current and voltage at the bridge. Revisit copper if the measured current or transient demand exceeds the available margin.

modelLimits: Prescribed passive current response does not predict the TPS62903 control loop.
Fixed-temperature switch models and estimated hot SOA extensions omit thermal accumulation.
Incomplete package, connector, cable and endpoint models prevent valid eye, BER or full-channel qualification.
Reset and VBUS models omit chip internals and powered-off input behavior.
Power budgets are accepted engineering assumptions, not measured bridge currents.
